A.explanation: A speed of $2.2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is about 100 times too small and ignores the correct conversion of $17\,000 \text{ km}$ and $78\,000 \text{ s}$.

B.explanation: Since $1 \text{ m} = 10^6 \text{ } \mu\text{m}$, $218 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ equals about $2.2 \times 10^8 \text{ } \mu\text{m s}^{-1}$, so $2.2 \times 10^7 \text{ } \mu\text{m s}^{-1}$ is too small by a factor of 10.

C.explanation: Since $1 \text{ m} = 10^9 \text{ nm}$, $218 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ equals about $2.2 \times 10^{11} \text{ nm s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: Since $1 \text{ m} = 10^3 \text{ mm}$, $218 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ equals about $2.2 \times 10^5 \text{ mm s}^{-1}$, so $2.2 \times 10^6 \text{ mm s}^{-1}$ is too large by a factor of 10.

hints: Convert the given time of 21 hours 40 minutes entirely to seconds and the distance of $17\,000 \text{ km}$ entirely to metres before dividing.
Use average speed $v = d/t$ to find the speed in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ - it should be a few hundred $\text{m s}^{-1}$ for a long-haul aircraft.
Check each prefix using $1 \text{ m} = 10^6 \text{ } \mu\text{m} = 10^9 \text{ nm} = 10^3 \text{ mm}$ and see which power of ten matches your $\text{m s}^{-1}$ value.
walkthrough: Convert the time to SI seconds: $t = 21 \times 3600 + 40 \times 60 = 75\,600 + 2\,400 = 78\,000 \text{ s}$.
Convert the distance to SI metres: $d = 17\,000 \text{ km} = 17\,000 \times 10^3 \text{ m} = 1.7 \times 10^7 \text{ m}$.
Calculate average speed with $v = d/t$: $v = (1.7 \times 10^7)/(7.8 \times 10^4) \approx 2.18 \times 10^2 \text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 218 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Convert metres to nanometres using $1 \text{ m} = 10^9 \text{ nm}$: $v \approx 218 \times 10^9 \text{ nm s}^{-1} = 2.18 \times 10^{11} \text{ nm s}^{-1}$, which to two significant figures is $2.2 \times 10^{11} \text{ nm s}^{-1}$.
The other prefixed options differ by a factor of 10 when converted back to $\text{m s}^{-1}$. This is option C.
